title: Director of Procurement

role_match.role_rationale_from_stage3: Given Grimco's extensive multi-location distribution network (65+ locations across US, Canada, UK) and broad overlaminate portfolio spanning vinyl, polyester, polycarbonate materials, the Director of Procurement manages supplier relationships, negotiates volume contracts, and optimizes the supply chain for their 611-employee operation. This role is critical because Grimco's business model depends on reliable access to differentiated products that their sign shop and vehicle wrap customers demand. Tedlar addresses key procurement priorities: (1) supplier reliability and product consistency across a national distribution footprint, (2) total cost of ownership advantages from reduced customer returns/warranty claims due to premature film failure, (3) premium margin opportunities that justify distribution investment, and (4) vendor partnership potential given DuPont's manufacturing scale and 60+ year track record. With Grimco actively showcasing innovations at ISA 2024 and Printing United 2023, procurement leadership would value adding a scientifically-proven protective film that enables competitive differentiation. The extreme temperature range (-70°F to 230°F), UV stability, and graffiti resistance solve practical field problems that reduce customer complaints and strengthen Grimco's value proposition to fabricators.

engagement_strategy.scope_and_authority: [Name] manages supplier relationships and vendor contracts across Grimco's 65+ locations in the US, Canada, and UK. This role owns supplier selection decisions, volume purchase negotiations, and supply chain optimization for their $241.8M operation. They report to C-suite (likely CFO or COO) and work cross-functionally with Product Management, Sales, and Operations. Their decisions directly impact inventory strategy, margin structure, and product availability across the entire distribution network. They evaluate new suppliers based on reliability, product differentiation potential, margin opportunity, and operational fit with Grimco's multi-location model.
engagement_strategy.relevant_use_cases: Tedlar overlaminates for outdoor signs and graphics address Grimco's core business—they distribute protective films for vehicle wraps, architectural graphics, outdoor signage, and floor protection. Specifically: (1) Vehicle wrap overlaminates that eliminate warranty claims from UV degradation and cracking that plague standard films; (2) Architectural building wrap films that withstand extreme weather across diverse North American climates (-70°F to 230°F range matters for Canada operations); (3) Graffiti-resistant overlaminates for transit graphics, municipal signage, and retail applications where vandalism creates costly replacement cycles for Grimco's customers; (4) Premium outdoor signage films that enable Grimco's fabricator customers to win high-value projects requiring validated performance specs. [Name]'s procurement team would benefit from reduced customer returns, fewer warranty disputes with end-users, and the ability to offer a scientifically-proven premium tier that competing distributors lack.
engagement_strategy.personal_stakes: [Name] is measured on: (1) Supplier reliability and fill rates across 65+ locations—product stockouts damage Grimco's reputation with fabricators; (2) Gross margin optimization—premium products with defensible differentiation command better margins than commodity overlaminates; (3) Total cost of quality—warranty claims and customer returns from film failures erode profitability and require procurement intervention; (4) Vendor relationship management—maintaining strong partnerships with manufacturers like 3M, Avery Dennison enables preferential pricing and allocation. Tedlar solves critical pain points: DuPont's manufacturing scale ensures consistent supply across their national footprint; the extreme durability reduces customer complaints that create operational headaches; the premium positioning justifies margin expansion; and the 60+ year brand heritage provides vendor partnership credibility. Failed overlaminates generate customer service escalations, returns processing costs, and damaged relationships with sign shops—problems that land on procurement's desk.
engagement_strategy.timing_factors: Grimco exhibited at ISA 2024 and Printing United 2023 showcasing innovations in protective films and partnered with Canon on equipment demonstrations—indicating active portfolio expansion in premium segments. Their 10 consecutive FASTSIGNS Vendor of the Year awards (through 2025) demonstrate commitment to supplier excellence and customer satisfaction, making them receptive to proven performance solutions. The sign and graphics industry is experiencing pressure from cheaper overseas competitors, creating urgency for distributors to differentiate through ultra-premium products that commodity suppliers cannot match. ISA Sign Expo 2026 is upcoming—ideal timing for procurement to evaluate new suppliers before major trade show commitments. Additionally, Grimco's multi-location expansion (65+ sites) creates operational complexity that favors reliable, high-performance suppliers who reduce supply chain friction.

personalization_hooks.hook: Grimco's 65-location distribution network across US, Canada, and UK creates complex supply chain demands where product consistency and supplier reliability are non-negotiable
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Open by acknowledging the operational challenge of maintaining quality standards across such a broad geographic footprint. Position Tedlar as solving the 'consistency problem' with DuPont's manufacturing scale and quality control systems that ensure identical performance whether shipped to Missouri or the UK. Frame the conversation around reducing supply chain risk rather than just adding another SKU.

personalization_hooks.hook: As a distributor carrying 3M, Avery Dennison, RTape, and Orafol overlaminates, Grimco may lack a true ultra-premium tier for customers demanding validated 15-20 year outdoor performance
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Reference their existing premium brand partnerships to establish credibility, then identify the portfolio gap—customers with architectural, municipal, or fleet projects requiring extreme performance specs that standard overlaminates cannot meet. Position Tedlar as the 'tier above' their current offerings, enabling Grimco to compete for projects they currently lose to specialty suppliers. Avoid criticizing existing vendors; frame as complementary positioning.

personalization_hooks.hook: 10 consecutive FASTSIGNS Vendor of the Year awards demonstrate Grimco's commitment to supplier excellence and solving fabricator pain points
personalization_hooks.messaging_angle: Lead with respect for their supplier reputation and customer-first approach. Connect Tedlar's graffiti resistance and UV stability directly to field problems their sign shop customers face—warranty callbacks, premature replacements, customer complaints about fading. Position the conversation as 'protecting Grimco's reputation by reducing the failure points that damage fabricator relationships.' This frames Tedlar as supporting their award-winning service model rather than just another product pitch.

recommended_approach: Lead with supply chain reliability and total cost of ownership angle. [Name] thinks operationally—focus on how Tedlar reduces downstream problems (warranty claims, customer returns, supply inconsistency) rather than leading with technical specs. Use the second personalization hook about portfolio gaps to create urgency, then support with DuPont's manufacturing credibility. Offer a brief exploratory call to understand their current overlaminate portfolio pain points before pitching Tedlar features. Procurement directors respond to business case logic and vendor partnership potential, not product enthusiasm.
